input.command: git status && git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD && git log -3 --oneline && git status -sb && ls -la artifacts && git check-ignore -v artifacts/audit.jsonl artifacts/notes.md || true
git remote -v && git branch -vv && git log --oneline -5 && git rev-parse HEAD && git merge-base HEAD origin/splitter/1111025706/r1/A 2>/dev/null; git branch -r | head -50

mkdir -p /opt/cursor/artifacts && node scratch/check.ts > /opt/cursor/artifacts/monthly-report-checks.log && node smoke.ts >> /opt/cursor/artifacts/monthly-report-checks.log && cat > /opt/cursor/artifacts/code-tour-author-handoff.md << 'EOF'
<decision>
Merchant-local calendar months, with net = gross sales − fees − refunds. Sales, fees, and refunds are positive sums of their own rows by `at`. The alternative was a UTC month, or net as gross − refunds with fees left off the bottom line; the request carries a timezone and no dates in the output, and a books close needs the cash residual.
</decision>
<risk>
Refunds are not tied back to a sale, so a refund larger than the original sale still counts in full. An unrecognized timezone or a bad `at` throws rather than returning zeros. Month matching is exact `YYYY-MM` in the merchant zone, so a non-padded month string would match nothing.
</risk>
<verified>
`node scratch/check.ts` (NY month edges, DST spring and fall, Kathmandu +5:45, UTC, issue-month refunds, negative net) and `node smoke.ts` (export loads; the fixture arguments do not match this function and are caught).
</verified>
EOF
echo "--- log ---" && cat /opt/cursor/artifacts/monthly-report-checks.log
git add impl.ts artifacts && git status && git diff --cached --stat && git commit -m "Implement ticket" && git status && git push -u origin HEAD && git status -sb
